influences.name: The Beatles
influences.context: ever since the Beatles started working with orchestras, it changed my mind about what was possible, what was credible for a rock act to do

influences.name: Segovia
influences.context: I was listening to Segovia and classical music, like a guilty pleasure thinking, 'Yeah, I love this stuff, but it's not gonna impact upon rock'

influences.name: Pink Floyd
influences.context: We lived opposite the Battersea Power Station, made famous many years by Pink Floyd and their flying pig

influences.name: Paul McCartney
influences.context: I was reading an old interview that Paul McCartney gave in the 1960s, I think it was for Life Magazine... 'Elenore Rigby' has a quality to it

influences.name: Dylan Thomas
influences.context: The famous line about 'Wearing a face that she keeps a job by the door' is something that was very Dylan Thomas-esque in a way because he would allude to certain things, the use of metaphor was important for him as a writer

influences.name: Bob Dylan
influences.context: By the mid-1960s, the influence of other Dylan, of course, is paramount upon the Beatles

influences.name: The Rolling Stones
influences.context: I was listening to The Stones very, very early on, and I love their work and practiced along with it relentlessly

influences.name: Charlie Watts
influences.context: when I was a kid, I desperately wanted to have the long hair that they had, and I thought out of all of them, Charlie was the most handsome

influences.name: Buddy Rich
influences.context: most drummers that I've talked to mentioned Buddy Rich in terms of saying, 'Well, yeah, this was the gospel handed down'

influences.name: Bach
influences.context: I'm influenced by masters like Bach, someone who had tremendous technique and complex underpinnings for every phrase, yet the musical effect is very simple because things are so focused.

influences.name: Anthony Phillips
influences.context: We all played 12-string and were fans of his sound. That was something we all shared in Genesis—the idea of lots of 12-strings all arpeggiating at once.

influences.name: Peter Green
influences.context: I read something recently in which Peter Green talked about filling Eric Clapton's shoes when he joined John Mayall's Bluesbreakers. He was under a lot of pressure with Eric being such a huge star. A difficult act to follow, even though Green was stunning in his own right.
